completed_milestones.summary: Environment audit, architecture and decision records, seven v1 contracts with examples and tests, olb CLI (validate, diagnose, check, state), roadmap and agent instructions.

World source tree with two working capabilities (text.stats, math.evaluate), a build-time capability invoker, olb world build and olb world verify, the digest algorithm, invocation protocol and data root default documented in CONTRACTS.md.

Simulation bootstrap: experiment manager, supervisor with deadline and process-tree termination, single hash-chained recorder, tool host, agent loop behind a ModelClient interface with a scripted stand-in, workspace artifact scanning, ols run and ols verify. No model is called.

Chat model client over Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with tool calling, tool-call repair, retry, context guard and recorded model identity; ols measure-model; llama3.2:3b measured and recorded in minimal world 0.2.0; one documented real-model run whose archive verifies.

Window bootstrap and first version: loopback-only standard-library server with a JSON API and a static front end (no build step). Run list, run summary with frozen configuration, paginated timeline with type filters, tool call and result pairs, artifact previews, live tail by polling, event-log check against the archive's own schemas and hash chain. Read-only guarantees are tested. Front-end stack decided (ADR-0008).

A reply without a tool call no longer ends a run: the runtime answers with the experiment's continuation message (default text in experiment-config 1.1.0), recorded as an environment.message event (observation-event 1.1.0); the context guard drops whole old turns and records it. Three candidate orchestrators (qwen3.5:2b, qwen3:4b, granite4.1:3b) pulled with authorisation, measured, recorded in minimal world 0.3.0 and compared with llama3.2:3b in eight archived open-trial runs. The Window renders environment.message.

Deterministic registry index, weighted pure-Python keyword search, complete generated capability documentation and three new simple capabilities (workspace.write, workspace.list, time.now). Minimal world 0.4.0 built, self-tested, verified and published; Simulation fixture rebuilt/copied, experiments updated and shipped tools tested (72c78d8). Scripted file-writing archive verified and text artifact inspected in the Window without changing archive bytes (9ef9ba4). Runtime discovery remains S005b.

known_issues.summary: WSL is installed but not functional on the development machine, and no container engine is present.
known_issues.detail: Repairing WSL 2 needs administrator rights. Until then only the process isolation tier is available. See ADR-0006.

known_issues.summary: FFmpeg and PyTorch are not installed.
The development machine is a laptop on a pre-release Windows build; sleep, updates and reboots will interrupt long runs.
known_issues.detail: Crash recovery (S006b) is mandatory. Power and update settings need review before multi-hour runs.

known_issues.summary: World builds, the content digest, process-tree termination and the Window have only been run on Windows.
known_issues.detail: The digest hashes stored bytes and the repository forces LF line endings, so it should be identical on Linux. The Simulation kills the run's process tree with a Job Object on Windows and a process group on POSIX; only the Windows path has been exercised. Check both the first time a Linux environment is available. The Window uses only pathlib and the standard-library HTTP server and should behave the same on Linux; its tests have not been run there.

known_issues.summary: On the process tier nothing stops a capability process from reading or writing outside the workspace.
known_issues.detail: The Simulation gives capabilities an empty environment and only tells them the workspace path, but that is a convention for Builder-written capabilities, not enforcement. The supervisor re-checks the world digest after each run. Real enforcement arrives with the container tier (S006c).

known_issues.summary: No local candidate that fits the 4 GB GPU behaves as an autonomous tool user under an unprompted premise.
known_issues.detail: Runs no longer end at the first reply without a tool call (S003c), but llama3.2:3b mostly applies text.stats to the text it was given and invents surroundings, and the other candidates ask for a task. See docs/experiments/2026-11-14-orchestrator-candidates.md and OD-2.

known_issues.summary: The context window in use is Ollama's default of 4096 tokens, and the server-reported input token count is not the conversation length.
known_issues.detail: The OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot set the context size per request. Since S003c the runtime blanks old tool results and then drops whole old turns (never the initial prompt), recording both, so nothing is cut silently; but with 4096 tokens the conversation keeps only a few recent turns. Long runs need a larger context (server setting or the native API) and memory.

known_issues.summary: Real image artifact previews remain unverified; synthetic image archives are tested.
known_issues.detail: S005a checked a real scripted workspace.write artifact in the Window: list metadata and preserved text preview displayed correctly, all 16 archive files were unchanged after browsing, and ols verify passed. No shipped capability creates an image yet. See docs/experiments/2026-11-14-registry-artifacts.md.

known_issues.summary: The Window cannot tell a run in progress from one that was interrupted, and its front end has no automated tests.
known_issues.detail: A run without summary.json is shown as 'not finished' with its last recorded state and last event time; nothing in the archive says whether the supervisor is still alive (S006b's recovery records could). The JSON API and the read-only guarantees are tested; rendering was checked by hand in a browser.

known_issues.summary: Thinking models spend most of their output budget on reasoning the record never sees, and it cannot be switched off through the endpoint in use.
known_issues.detail: max_output_tokens covers the hidden reasoning: qwen3:4b at 512 produced only empty replies. Asking Ollama 0.40.16 for reasoning_effort 'none' moved the reasoning into the reply text, which would be recorded as said, so the runtime sends no such option. If a thinking model is chosen (OD-2) the protocol must say how much unrecorded computation is acceptable.

open_decisions.summary: Container mechanism for the container isolation tier (Podman in WSL 2 preferred).
open_decisions.detail: Decide once WSL is repaired and the options can be tested. ADR-0006.

open_decisions.summary: Which orchestrator model to use. Four models that fit the 4 GB GPU have been compared; none behaves as an autonomous tool user unprompted.
open_decisions.detail: Evidence in docs/experiments/2026-11-14-orchestrator-candidates.md. llama3.2:3b uses tools most but invents surroundings; qwen3:4b is grounded but needs about 2048 output tokens per reply (hidden reasoning, about 30 s per step); qwen3.5:2b and granite4.1:3b act as assistants waiting for a user. Options: keep llama3.2:3b, adopt qwen3:4b with a larger output limit, authorise a larger partially offloaded model (e.g. qwen3.5:4b or qwen3.5:9b), or enable an external provider (ADR-0005). Worth repeating after S005b, when the world has more tools. Deferred by the human on 2026-11-14: llama3.2:3b stays the default for now. Planned later: try a larger model, and a 'brain swap' mode that can use an external provider with the human's own API key (a frontier model, or a hosted Gemma model) - see the note under S007a in ROADMAP.md.
